REGULATORY SANDBOX APPLICATION

Applicant: ZimAssure Ltd
Application Date: 15 March 2026
Submitted to: Insurance and Pensions Commission (IPEC)

1. PROBLEM STATEMENT
ZimAssure Ltd seeks to test a parametric micro-insurance product for smallholder farmers in Mashonaland West. The existing regulatory framework under the Insurance Act [Chapter 24:07] does not accommodate automatic trigger-based claims settlement without a formal loss assessment. This regulatory gap prevents deployment of our weather-index insurance solution.

2. BUSINESS MODEL
The product uses satellite weather data to trigger automatic payouts when rainfall falls below a defined threshold. Premiums are collected via mobile money platforms including EcoCash and OneMoney. Target customers are smallholder farmers with landholdings between 0.5 and 5 hectares.

3. TESTING PLAN
Proposed testing period: 12 months commencing Q3 2026. Target customer base limited to 500 farmers in Chinhoyi district. Transaction limit of USD 500 per payout per farmer per season. Key performance indicators include claim processing time under 48 hours and customer satisfaction score above 80%.

4. BOUNDARY CONDITIONS
Geographical location: Chinhoyi district, Mashonaland West. Start and end date: 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027. Number of customers: maximum 500 enrolled participants. Consent to participate will be obtained in writing before enrolment.

5. REGULATORY RELIEF SOUGHT
ZimAssure Ltd requests relaxation of Section 45 of the Insurance Act to permit trigger-based settlements without a formal loss adjuster assessment during the testing period.

IPEC REGULATORY SANDBOX APPLICATION FORM

Participant: Harare Mutual Insurance
Date: 2 February 2026

1. INNOVATION DESCRIPTION
Harare Mutual Insurance proposes to test a blockchain-based claims ledger that automates subrogation recoveries between insurers. The innovation addresses inefficiencies in the current manual claims reconciliation process, which results in delays exceeding 90 days. No existing licence category accommodates a shared distributed ledger among multiple IPEC-regulated entities.

2. GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE
The applicant is a registered short-term insurer licensed by IPEC. Shareholders include Harare City Pension Fund (40%) and private investors (60%). The Board of Directors comprises five members including two independent non-executive directors. An organogram and beneficial owner declarations are attached as Annexure A.

3. REGULATORY APPROVAL REQUIREMENT
Commission approval is required under Section 12 of the Insurance and Pensions Commission Act to permit data sharing between regulated entities. The sandbox would grant a conditional approval for the duration of the testing period.

4. TESTING PLAN AND KPIs
Testing period: 6 months. Key performance indicators: reduction in subrogation settlement time from 90 to 30 days; recovery rate improvement from 45% to 65%. Success criteria include zero security incidents and zero customer data breaches.

5. EXIT PLAN
At graduation phase, the blockchain ledger will transition to a fully licensed shared infrastructure. An exit report will be submitted to IPEC within 30 days of test conclusion.

APPLICATION FOR REGULATORY SANDBOX PARTICIPATION

Applicant Entity: Victoria Falls Reinsurance Ltd
Registered Address: 14 Livingstone Avenue, Harare, Zimbabwe
Date of Application: 10 January 2026

SECTION A — SCOPE AND MANDATE
Victoria Falls Reinsurance Ltd operates within the purview of IPEC as a registered reinsurer under the Insurance Act [Chapter 24:07]. The proposed innovation is a real-time risk aggregation dashboard that enables proportional reinsurance treaties to be adjusted automatically based on live exposure data.

SECTION B — REGULATORY GAP
The existing framework does not permit mid-period treaty amendments without formal Commission approval. Our solution requires dynamic adjustment of retention levels, which cannot operate within current treaty reporting requirements.

SECTION C — CAPACITY TO PARTICIPATE
Business model: SaaS platform integrated with IPEC quarterly return submissions. Testing plan includes three milestones: integration (Month 1-2), parallel running (Month 3-4), and full deployment assessment (Month 5-6). Resources allocated include a dedicated technical team of four engineers and a compliance officer.

SECTION D — FIT AND PROPER REQUIREMENTS
All directors have submitted police clearance certificates and tax clearance certificates. The company has no record of money laundering or financial crime. No director is an insolvent person.

SECTION E — KPI TARGETS
Key performance indicator 1: system uptime above 99.5%. KPI 2: data reconciliation accuracy above 99.9%. KPI 3: Commission reporting latency below 4 hours.

SANDBOX APPLICATION — ZimTech Insurance Solutions

Executive Summary: ZimTech Insurance Solutions seeks approval to test a digital insurance marketplace connecting micro-SMEs with short-term insurers. The platform aggregates quotes in real time and processes premiums via ZIPIT transfer. The innovation is not covered under any existing IPEC licence category as it operates as a price comparison and binding authority platform simultaneously.

Testing Parameters:
- Duration of the test: 9 months
- Target customer type: SMEs with turnover below USD 500,000 per annum
- Geographical location: Harare and Bulawayo metropolitan areas
- Transaction limit: USD 10,000 per policy
- Number of customers: maximum 1,000 businesses

KPI Framework:
- Customer acquisition cost below USD 25
- Policy issuance within 2 minutes of quote acceptance
- Claims notification within 24 hours
- Net Promoter Score above 70

Regulatory Relief Required:
Relaxation of the intermediary licensing requirements under Section 28 of the Insurance Act to allow algorithmic quote binding during the testing period.

Safeguards:
All customer data processed in accordance with Know Your Customer requirements. Anti-Money Laundering checks performed at onboarding. Treating Customers Fairly principles applied throughout the test.

Consent to participate will be obtained electronically with biometric verification.

REGULATORY SANDBOX APPLICATION
Applicant: Gweru Life Assurance Company
Product: Pay-as-you-live life insurance with wearable device integration

PROBLEM STATEMENT
Gweru Life Assurance Company proposes to test a usage-based life assurance product that adjusts premiums monthly based on health data collected from wearables. The Insurance Act [Chapter 24:07] does not contemplate variable premium life policies. Regulatory approval is required to operate a product with monthly premium variability outside fixed-premium actuarial tables.

BUSINESS MODEL DESCRIPTION
Premiums are adjusted monthly within a band of +/-20% of the base premium based on health KPIs (steps, heart rate, sleep). Policyholders who meet health targets receive discounts. The product targets employed professionals aged 25-45 in Harare.

BOUNDARY CONDITIONS
Start and end date: 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. Number of customers: 300 policyholders. Geographical location: Harare metropolitan area. Transaction limit: maximum monthly premium of USD 200 per policyholder.

GOVERNANCE
Shareholders: Gweru Holdings (70%), Management (30%). Directors list and organogram attached. Beneficial owner: Dr. S. Moyo (principal). Police clearance and tax clearance certificates attached.

MILESTONES
- Month 1-3: Device integration and onboarding
- Month 4-9: Active testing with quarterly reporting to IPEC
- Month 10-12: Graduation phase assessment and exit report

APPLICATION TO PARTICIPATE IN THE IPEC REGULATORY SANDBOX

Applicant: Mutare Digital Brokers (Pvt) Ltd
Date: 5 March 2026

INNOVATION SUMMARY
Mutare Digital Brokers proposes a conversational AI insurance assistant that guides rural customers through claims notification via SMS and WhatsApp. The existing framework requires physical claims notification which is inaccessible to rural customers. This regulatory gap prevents us from deploying the solution under any existing licence category.

CAPACITY EVIDENCE
Business model: B2B2C model — the assistant is white-labelled to licensed insurers. Testing plan: 3 phases over 12 months with IPEC milestone reporting. KPI targets include 90% claims notification success rate and average handling time below 5 minutes. Resources: technology team of 6, partnerships with 3 licensed insurers.

REGULATORY WAIVER
Exemption sought: relaxation of the written claims notification requirement under Motor Third Party regulations to permit digital notification during the testing period.

FIT AND PROPER
All principals hold valid police clearance certificates. Tax clearance certificates attached. No director is an insolvent person or has been convicted of money laundering.

CUSTOMER SAFEGUARDS
Treating Customers Fairly policy implemented. Dispute resolution mechanism includes escalation to IPEC within 14 days. Know Your Customer verification via national ID number at onboarding.

IPEC SANDBOX APPLICATION — SECTION SUMMARY

Applicant: Bulawayo Agri-Insurance Co.
Innovation: Index-based crop insurance with satellite trigger

This application is submitted in accordance with the IPEC Regulatory Sandbox Guidelines effective Q4 2025. Bulawayo Agri-Insurance Co. is an entity registered under the Insurance Act [Chapter 24:07] and falls under the supervisory purview of the Insurance and Pensions Commission.

The applicant cannot operate within the existing framework because index insurance products with automatic payouts are not recognised under current policy wording standards. The regulatory gap arises because no existing licence covers parametric trigger settlements.

Proposed testing period: 6 months. The test will involve 200 farmers in Matabeleland South. Boundary conditions include: transaction limit of USD 300 per trigger event; consent to participate obtained before enrolment; geographical location restricted to Gwanda district.

KPI success criteria: payout processing time under 72 hours; basis risk below 15%; customer retention above 75% at end of testing period.

Governance: company directors and shareholders declared. Organogram attached. Beneficial owner: Mr. T. Ndlovu. Police clearance and tax clearance submitted.

Regulatory relief: relaxation of the loss assessment requirement under IPEC Circular 14/2022 during the 6-month testing window.

SANDBOX APPLICATION — ZimAssure Digital Health Division

Product Name: TeleCare Health Shield
Applicant: ZimAssure Ltd (Health Division)
Submission Date: 20 February 2026

1. PROBLEM STATEMENT AND REGULATORY GAP
ZimAssure seeks to test a telemedicine-linked health insurance product that includes real-time pre-authorisation for outpatient consultations via a mobile app. No existing IPEC licence category covers real-time pre-authorisation integrated with telemedicine. The existing regulatory approval framework requires prior written Commission approval for each pre-authorisation protocol change.

2. BUSINESS MODEL
Premiums collected monthly via direct debit. Target customer type: formally employed workers in Harare and Chitungwiza. Coverage: outpatient, inpatient, and dental. Pre-authorisation response time: under 60 seconds.

3. TESTING PLAN
Duration of the test: 12 months. KPIs: pre-authorisation accuracy above 95%; claims rejection rate below 5%; customer satisfaction above 85%. Milestones at Month 3, 6, and 9 with IPEC quarterly reports.

4. EXIT PLAN
At the graduation phase, the pre-authorisation algorithm will be submitted for formal actuarial review. Post-exit, the product transitions to a standard health insurance licence. An orderly exit protocol is in place if the test is discontinued early.

5. SAFEGUARDS
Know Your Customer checks at enrolment. Anti-Money Laundering monitoring on premium transactions above USD 1,000. Complaints handled within 5 business days. Treating Customers Fairly framework implemented.

REGULATORY SANDBOX APPLICATION
Applicant: Pan-Africa Micro-Finance Insurance Ltd (PAMFIL)
Date: 1 April 2026

INTRODUCTION
PAMFIL is a Fintech entity seeking to test an embedded insurance product distributed through a mobile lending platform. The innovation provides automatic credit-life cover triggered at loan disbursement. IPEC's existing regulations do not contemplate embedded insurance distribution via non-insurance platforms. Commission approval is required before PAMFIL can legally distribute policies.

BOUNDARY CONDITIONS
Testing period: 6 months. Start and end date: 1 May 2026 to 31 October 2026. Target customer type: mobile lending borrowers with loans between USD 50 and USD 500. Number of customers: 2,000 borrowers. Geographical location: nationwide digital distribution.

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS
KPI 1: policy issuance rate above 90% of eligible borrowers; KPI 2: claims settlement within 7 days of death notification; KPI 3: lapse rate below 10%.

FIT AND PROPER
Shareholders and directors declared. Police clearance and tax clearance attached. No director is insolvent or has been involved in money laundering.

REGULATORY RELIEF SOUGHT
Exemption sought from the intermediary licensing requirement to allow the lending platform to distribute policies as an embedded feature during the testing period. Relaxation will expire at the end of the 6-month test.

EXIT PLAN
Orderly exit: all active policies novated to a licensed insurer. Exit report submitted to IPEC within 14 days of test conclusion.

SANDBOX APPLICATION SUMMARY — HARARE PENSION TECH (HPT)

Applicant: Harare Pension Tech Ltd
Innovation: Automated pension drawdown calculator with regulatory override

HPT proposes to test an AI-powered pension drawdown optimisation tool for occupational pension funds. The tool recommends drawdown amounts that may deviate from the statutory minimum drawdown tables under the Pensions and Provident Funds Act [Chapter 24:32]. This cannot operate within the current framework without Commission approval.

Scope and mandate: The innovation falls within the purview of IPEC's pension supervisory mandate. Commission oversight applies throughout the testing period.

Governance: HPT is a Fintech entity incorporated in Zimbabwe. Beneficial owner: Ms. R. Chigumbura. Directors: three members. Police clearance and tax clearance certificates submitted. No director is an insolvent person.

Testing plan: 9 months, 50 pension funds, 500 members. Key performance indicator: member drawdown adequacy score above 80% versus baseline. Milestones at Month 3, 6, and 9.

Regulatory waiver: relaxation of the fixed drawdown table requirement for participating funds during the 9-month testing period.

Customer safeguards: Treating Customers Fairly principles apply. All members to provide written consent to participate before enrolment. Dispute resolution escalation within 7 days.

REGULATORY SANDBOX APPLICATION
Applicant: Zimnat Digital (Pvt) Ltd
Date: 12 March 2026

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Zimnat Digital proposes to test a P2P risk-pooling product for informal traders in Harare's Mbare market. Participants pool premiums via a mobile app and share losses according to pre-agreed rules. This model is not covered under any existing IPEC licence as mutual associations of this type are not recognised under the Insurance Act [Chapter 24:07].

REGULATORY GAP
Zimnat Digital cannot operate within the existing framework because P2P risk pooling without a licensed insurer as risk carrier has no regulatory basis. The innovation requires a temporary exemption from the insurer capital adequacy requirements.

BOUNDARY CONDITIONS
Testing period: 6 months. Number of customers: 300 traders. Transaction limit: USD 50 per member per month. Start and end date: 1 June 2026 to 30 November 2026. Geographical location: Mbare district, Harare.

KPIs AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
Success criteria: pool adequacy ratio above 110%; average claim settlement 3 days; member satisfaction above 75%.

FIT AND PROPER REQUIREMENTS
Police clearance and tax clearance for all directors attached. No insolvent person on the board. No history of money laundering or CFT violations.

SAFEGUARDS
KYC checks at member registration. Anti-Money Laundering transaction monitoring. Treating Customers Fairly framework and complaints procedure in place.

APPLICATION TO THE IPEC REGULATORY SANDBOX
Applicant: Victoria Falls Reinsurance Ltd — Facultative Division
Date: 20 April 2026

INNOVATION: Dynamic Facultative Pricing Engine

The applicant proposes to test a machine-learning-based facultative reinsurance pricing engine that generates real-time risk scores and pricing for large individual risks. The existing reinsurance treaty framework requires manual underwriting sign-off, which cannot accommodate automated pricing within a 4-hour turnaround requirement.

SCOPE: This application falls within the supervisory mandate of IPEC as the innovation relates to insurance activities (reinsurance underwriting).

GOVERNANCE: Victoria Falls Reinsurance Ltd is a registered reinsurer under the Insurance Act. Directors declared. Organogram attached. Beneficial owner: VFR Holdings Ltd. Police clearance and tax clearance attached.

TESTING PLAN: 12-month testing period. KPI targets: pricing accuracy within 5% of manual underwriter benchmark; quote turnaround under 4 hours; zero regulatory compliance incidents.

REGULATORY APPROVAL: Commission approval is required under Section 20 of the Insurance Act to permit algorithmic underwriting without manual sign-off.

EXIT PLAN: Graduation phase at Month 10-12. Post-exit, the engine becomes a licensed underwriting support tool. Exit report submitted within 21 days of test conclusion.

SANDBOX APPLICATION — MASVINGO FUNERAL ASSURERS CO-OPERATIVE
Date: 8 January 2026

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Masvingo Funeral Assurers Co-operative seeks to test a community-based funeral assurance product distributed via church networks in Masvingo Province. The product collects weekly contributions via church tithe systems. This distribution model has no existing regulatory basis under the Funeral Assurers Act.

PROBLEM STATEMENT
The Co-operative cannot operate within the existing regulatory framework because the use of church networks as distribution agents is not contemplated by any IPEC licence category. A regulatory gap exists between the product concept and current licensing requirements.

BOUNDARY CONDITIONS
Testing period: 6 months. Number of customers: 1,000 church members across 10 congregations. Transaction limit: USD 5 per week per member. Start and end date: 1 July 2026 to 31 December 2026. Geographical location: Masvingo district. Consent to participate obtained at congregation level.

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS
KPI 1: membership retention above 80%; KPI 2: claim settlement within 48 hours of death notification; KPI 3: premium collection rate above 90%.

FIT AND PROPER
Police clearance: all committee members. Tax clearance: co-operative registered taxpayer. No insolvent person on the committee.

SAFEGUARDS
Know Your Customer at enrolment. Complaints escalation to IPEC. Treating Customers Fairly framework adopted.

REGULATORY SANDBOX APPLICATION
Applicant: ZimAssure Ltd — AgriTech Division
Product: Livestock mortality index insurance
Date: 15 April 2026

The AgriTech Division of ZimAssure Ltd applies for admission to the IPEC Regulatory Sandbox to test a livestock mortality index insurance product for cattle farmers in Midlands Province. The product pays out automatically when livestock mortality in a defined area exceeds a pre-set threshold derived from satellite imagery and veterinary records. This innovation cannot operate within the existing Insurance Act framework because there is no regulatory basis for area-yield or area-mortality index insurance.

Regulatory waiver required: exemption sought from the individual loss assessment requirement for each claim, allowing area-level trigger assessment instead.

Testing parameters: 6-month testing period; 400 cattle farmers; Kwekwe district; transaction limit USD 800 per farm per trigger event.

KPIs: basis risk below 20%; payout processing within 5 days of trigger confirmation; farmer satisfaction above 70%.

Governance: ZimAssure Ltd is a licensed short-term insurer. Shareholders and directors declared. Police clearance and tax clearance attached. No beneficial owner is an insolvent person.

Exit plan: at graduation phase, the product is submitted for full actuarial review and standard product approval. An orderly exit is guaranteed by reinsurance treaty with Victoria Falls Reinsurance.

APPLICATION FOR REGULATORY SANDBOX
Applicant: Harare Mutual Insurance — Cyber Division
Date: 3 March 2026

INNOVATION: Real-time cyber risk scoring and dynamic cyber insurance

Harare Mutual Insurance proposes to test a cyber insurance product whose premiums are dynamically adjusted monthly based on a real-time cyber risk score derived from the policyholder's network vulnerability scans. This cannot operate within the existing framework because the Insurance Act requires actuarially certified fixed premium tables for all non-life products.

Regulatory gap: no existing licence category contemplates dynamic, vulnerability-linked premium adjustment for cyber insurance.

Testing period: 12 months. Target customer type: SMEs with IT infrastructure in Harare. Number of customers: 150 SMEs. Transaction limit: USD 5,000 monthly premium.

KPI targets: claim frequency reduction of 15% versus static-premium benchmark; customer renewal rate above 80%; vulnerability score improvement of 10% average across the cohort.

Governance: Harare Mutual Insurance is a licensed insurer. Directors declared. Beneficial owner: Harare City Council Pension Fund. Police clearance and tax clearance submitted.

Regulatory relief: relaxation of the fixed premium certification requirement for the 12-month testing window. Commission approval is required before the test commences.

Exit conditions: post-exit, premiums revert to certified actuarial tables pending formal approval of dynamic pricing model.

IPEC SANDBOX APPLICATION — FULL SUBMISSION
Applicant: NovaBridge Insurance Intermediaries
Date: 17 February 2026

NovaBridge Insurance Intermediaries applies to test an insurance product comparison and instant-bind platform that integrates with five licensed insurers via API. The platform is not covered under any existing intermediary licence as it combines price comparison, instant binding authority, and real-time premium collection.

Scope: activities fall within IPEC's insurance supervisory mandate under the Insurance Act [Chapter 24:07].

Capacity to participate: business model is B2B2C via licensed insurer partnerships. Testing plan includes three phases: API integration (Month 1), soft launch to 100 test customers (Month 2-4), and full pilot with 500 customers (Month 5-9). Key performance indicator: policy issuance within 3 minutes; error rate below 1%; customer complaint rate below 2%.

Regulatory approval requirement: Commission approval under the intermediary licence provisions is required. The sandbox provides conditional approval for the 9-month testing period.

Fit and proper: directors' police clearance and tax clearance submitted. No director is an insolvent person. No money laundering history.

Boundary conditions: 500 customers maximum; Harare and Bulawayo; transaction limit USD 20,000 per policy.

Exit plan: orderly exit via transfer of all bound policies to individual insurer direct books. Exit report within 30 days.

SANDBOX APPLICATION — ZIMBABWE HEALTH FINTECH (ZHF)
Date: 28 January 2026

PRODUCT: Community health micro-savings and insurance hybrid

Zimbabwe Health Fintech proposes to test a hybrid savings-insurance product for low-income households in Chitungwiza. Members save weekly into a pool that provides health cover for up to USD 500 per illness episode. This product is not covered under any existing IPEC licence as it combines savings and insurance without being a formal pension fund.

Problem statement: ZHF cannot operate within the existing regulatory framework because hybrid savings-insurance products for low-income households have no licensing pathway under either the Insurance Act or the Pensions and Provident Funds Act.

Testing parameters: 9-month testing period; 600 households; Chitungwiza North ward; weekly contribution of USD 2 per household; transaction limit USD 500 per illness episode.

KPIs: claim settlement within 3 days; pool adequacy maintained above 120%; member retention above 75%.

Governance: ZHF is incorporated as a private limited company. Directors declared. Beneficial owner: Dr. A. Chikwanda. Police clearance and tax clearance attached.

Safeguards: Know Your Customer at household level; Anti-Money Laundering monitoring; Treating Customers Fairly framework adopted; complaints handled within 5 days.

REGULATORY SANDBOX APPLICATION
Applicant: Digital Reinsurance Solutions (DRS)
Date: 22 March 2026

INNOVATION: Automated proportional treaty settlement

DRS proposes a blockchain-based smart contract system that automates quarterly settlement calculations for proportional reinsurance treaties. The system eliminates manual bordereaux reconciliation. The existing IPEC reinsurance framework requires manual submission of bordereaux within 45 days of quarter end, which this system replaces with real-time settlement.

Regulatory gap: smart contract settlement has no basis in current treaty regulations. DRS cannot operate within the existing framework without Commission approval.

Boundary conditions: 6-month testing period; 5 participating IPEC-licensed insurers; transaction value limit of USD 2 million per quarter per insurer.

KPIs: settlement discrepancy rate below 0.1%; processing time reduction from 45 days to 5 days; zero security incidents.

Governance: DRS is a Fintech entity registered in Zimbabwe. Directors and shareholders declared. Beneficial owner: Digital Africa Holdings. Police clearance and tax clearance submitted. No insolvent person on the board.

Regulatory relief: waiver of the manual bordereaux submission requirement under IPEC Circular 32/2023 for participating insurers during the testing period.

Exit plan: at graduation phase, the smart contract protocol is submitted to IPEC for formal recognition as an approved settlement method. Orderly exit provisions include manual reconciliation fallback.

IPEC REGULATORY SANDBOX — APPLICATION
Applicant: Midlands Life Assurance Ltd
Date: 4 April 2026

SUMMARY OF INNOVATION
Midlands Life proposes to test an automated life underwriting engine for group life schemes, enabling same-day policy issuance for schemes of up to 500 members without individual medical evidence. The existing framework requires medical evidence for group life policies above 100 members.

Problem statement: the regulatory constraint prevents same-day onboarding of larger employer groups, reducing competitiveness against regional insurers.

Testing plan: 12-month testing period. Milestones: Month 1-3 data integration; Month 4-8 active testing; Month 9-12 graduation phase assessment. Key performance indicators: underwriting decision accuracy within 2% of manual benchmark; fraud incidence below industry average; scheme lapse rate below 8%.

Boundary conditions: 20 employer groups; 5,000 lives maximum; Harare and Gweru locations; transaction limit USD 500,000 sum assured per member.

Governance: Midlands Life is a registered life assurer. Directors declared. Shareholders: Midlands Province Development Fund (35%), private investors (65%). Police clearance and tax clearance submitted.

Regulatory relief: relaxation of the medical evidence threshold from 100 to 500 members for the 12-month test duration.

Safeguards: all members sign written consent to participate. Dispute resolution within 10 business days. Treating Customers Fairly framework enforced.

SANDBOX APPLICATION COVER SHEET
Applicant: AfriGrow Insurance Technology
Date: 18 March 2026

AfriGrow Insurance Technology applies to participate in the IPEC Regulatory Sandbox with a product that provides automatic trade credit insurance for cross-border SME transactions within the SADC region. The product uses buyer credit scores derived from banking transaction histories to automate underwriting decisions.

Scope: the innovation falls within IPEC's insurance supervisory mandate as a short-term insurance product.

Regulatory approval requirement: Commission approval is required because cross-border trade credit insurance using algorithmic underwriting has no existing regulatory basis under the Insurance Act.

Business model: premiums collected per shipment, integrated with commercial bank letters of credit. Target customer type: SMEs exporting to SADC markets. Number of customers: 100 SMEs. Testing period: 9 months.

KPIs: claims accuracy rate above 90%; average underwriting decision time under 10 minutes; customer complaint rate below 3%.

Fit and proper: directors declared. Police clearance and tax clearance submitted. Beneficial owner: AfriGrow Capital Holdings. No insolvent person on the board. No money laundering history.

Boundary conditions: geographical location — Harare and Bulawayo export hubs; transaction limit USD 50,000 per shipment; consent to participate obtained from each SME.

REGULATORY SANDBOX APPLICATION — FINAL PAGE
Applicant: Southern Cross Medical Aid Society
Date: 25 March 2026

Southern Cross Medical Aid Society seeks sandbox approval to test a capitation-based primary healthcare model integrated with its medical aid product. Under capitation, a fixed monthly fee per member is paid to a clinic regardless of utilisation. The current regulatory framework for medical aid societies does not accommodate capitation arrangements, requiring fee-for-service reimbursement only.

The innovation cannot operate within the existing regulatory framework because capitation contracts constitute risk transfer from the society to the clinic, which is not recognised under current IPEC medical aid regulations.

Testing period: 12 months. 1,000 members. Harare North clinic network. Transaction limit: USD 50 per member per month capitation fee.

KPIs: hospital admission rate reduction target of 15%; member satisfaction above 80%; capitation budget variance below 5%.

Governance: Southern Cross is registered under the Medical Aid Societies Act. Council members declared. Beneficial owner structure disclosed. Police clearance and tax clearance submitted.

Regulatory relief: relaxation of the fee-for-service requirement to permit capitation payments to contracted clinics during the 12-month testing period.

Exit conditions: post-exit evaluation by IPEC determines whether capitation is incorporated into the Medical Aid Societies Regulations. Orderly exit provisions include reversion to fee-for-service pending formal approval.

IPEC REGULATORY SANDBOX APPLICATION — SECTION 7
Applicant: ZimCredit Life Assurance
Date: 10 February 2026

ZimCredit Life Assurance proposes to test an automated lender-placed credit-life insurance product embedded in mobile lending applications. When a borrower is approved, cover is automatically placed without a separate insurance application. The Insurance Act does not contemplate automatic placement without explicit policyholder consent documented in a signed proposal form.

Regulatory gap: automatic lender-placed cover conflicts with the signed proposal form requirement under Section 53 of the Insurance Act.

Business model: premiums deducted from loan disbursements. Target customer type: mobile money borrowers. Number of customers: 5,000 borrowers. Testing period: 6 months. Transaction limit: USD 100 per policy.

KPIs: policy placement rate above 95%; claim settlement within 5 days; no regulatory complaints from borrowers.

Governance: ZimCredit is a licensed life insurer. Directors declared. Beneficial owner: ZimCredit Holdings. Police clearance and tax clearance submitted.

Regulatory relief: exemption sought from the signed proposal form requirement for lender-placed cover during the 6-month testing window, subject to digital consent recording.

Safeguards: Know Your Customer at loan origination. Anti-Money Laundering screening. Treating Customers Fairly framework applied. Complaints procedure disclosed to all borrowers.

REGULATORY SANDBOX APPLICATION FORM — PAGE 1 OF 3
Applicant: Harare Mutual Insurance — Property Division
Product: Parametric property insurance for flood risk
Date: 14 April 2026

Harare Mutual Insurance proposes to test a parametric flood insurance product for commercial properties in Harare's low-lying industrial areas. The product pays out automatically when official flood gauges exceed a defined threshold, without requiring a loss adjuster visit. This cannot operate within the existing Insurance Act framework because automatic settlement without a formal loss assessment is not permitted.

Regulatory gap: the non-life insurance regulations require a licensed loss adjuster to assess each claim. Parametric triggers bypass this requirement.

Boundary conditions: start and end date 1 August 2026 to 31 January 2027; 50 commercial properties; Willowvale and Workington industrial areas; transaction limit USD 20,000 per trigger event.

KPIs: trigger accuracy within 10% of actual flood damage; payout within 24 hours of trigger; customer satisfaction above 75%.

Governance: Harare Mutual is a licensed non-life insurer. Directors declared. Beneficial owner: Harare City Council Pension Fund. Police clearance and tax clearance submitted.

Regulatory relief: waiver of the loss adjuster requirement for parametric products during the 6-month testing period.

Exit plan: at graduation, the parametric product seeks formal certification under IPEC's product approval process. Orderly exit ensured by reinsurance backing.

SANDBOX APPLICATION — MASVINGO DIGITAL INSURERS
Date: 6 March 2026

Masvingo Digital Insurers applies to test an on-demand short-term insurance product for gig workers delivered entirely via a USSD platform. Cover is purchased per shift (minimum 4 hours) and expires automatically. The existing short-term insurance framework requires annual or monthly policy periods and does not accommodate per-shift micro-duration cover.

Regulatory gap: per-shift cover periods have no basis in IPEC's current policy wording standards. Masvingo Digital cannot operate within the existing framework without a special dispensation.

Testing parameters: 6-month testing period; 1,000 gig workers; Harare, Bulawayo, Mutare; transaction limit USD 5 per shift per worker.

KPIs: policy issuance within 30 seconds of USSD request; claim notification within 2 hours of incident; customer complaint rate below 1%.

Governance: Masvingo Digital Insurers is a licensed short-term insurer. Directors declared. Beneficial owner: Southern Capital Group. Police clearance and tax clearance submitted.

Regulatory relief: relaxation of the minimum policy period requirement to permit per-shift cover during the 6-month test.

Safeguards: Know Your Customer via national ID at registration. Treating Customers Fairly framework. Dispute resolution via IPEC escalation within 5 days. Consent to participate recorded at registration.

IPEC REGULATORY SANDBOX APPLICATION
Applicant: First Fidelity Life Assurance
Date: 30 March 2026

First Fidelity Life Assurance applies to test a tontine-linked savings and assurance product for diaspora Zimbabweans sending remittances. Participants contribute monthly and the pool grows; upon death, dependants receive a pre-agreed lump sum. The product has characteristics of both a life assurance contract and an informal savings club, which has no existing regulatory category.

Problem statement: tontine-linked products are not recognised under the Insurance Act or the Pensions and Provident Funds Act. First Fidelity cannot operate within the existing framework.

Testing period: 12 months. 200 diaspora members. Digital platform (online). Transaction limit USD 100 per month per member.

KPIs: member retention rate above 85%; fund growth above inflation; death benefit processing within 14 days.

Governance: First Fidelity is a licensed life assurer. Directors declared. Beneficial owner: First Fidelity Holdings. Police clearance and tax clearance submitted. No insolvent person.

Regulatory relief: exemption from the formal policy wording requirements for tontine products during the 12-month testing period.

Safeguards: Know Your Customer via biometric verification. Anti-Money Laundering monitoring. Treating Customers Fairly. Complaints resolution within 7 days. Consent to participate signed digitally.

REGULATORY SANDBOX APPLICATION — COVER PAGE
Applicant: Victoria Falls Reinsurance Ltd — Life Division
Date: 19 April 2026

VFR Life proposes to test a mortality-linked catastrophe bond structure that transfers pandemic mortality risk to capital markets. IPEC's existing reinsurance framework does not contemplate capital market risk transfer instruments. Commission approval is required before any such structure can be operated.
